overall_summary: Deduplication reveals 47 unique Shorts. Performance is heavily polarized: first-person hypothetical space survival hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') and counterintuitive planetary paradoxes ('Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year') generate the highest velocity, consistently surpassing 800-1,000 views with strong engagement (up to 38 likes). In contrast, generic psychology facts ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and repeated uploads of identical concepts ('Why Space Is Completely Silent') consistently stall under 100 views with near-zero engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Cosmic Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (825 views, 15 likes) dramatically outperform third-person planet fact videos.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme astronomical and space phenomena through immediate, sensory first-person POV survival scenarios rather than passive encyclopedic trivia.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' exploded to 970 views and 21 likes within ~30 hours of publishing, leading recent 7-day velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Open with high-contrast, seemingly impossible physical realities that shatter common-sense physics within the first 2 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple variations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' and song-stuck-in-head videos averaged under 40 views with 0 comments and negligible likes.
weak_patterns.action: Retire generic brain/psychology trivia unless connected to an intense cinematic micro-drama or high-stakes mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Third-person titles like 'The Planet Where It Rains Liquid Metal!' (10 views) and 'The Planet Where It Rains Rock!' (50 views) flopped compared to active POV framing of similar worlds.
weak_patterns.action: Never lead with 'The Planet Where It Rains X'; convert the hook into experiential peril or a high-stakes comparative paradox.
